display.name: Karpenter Monitoring
display.description: Tracks the Karpenter fleet, scheduling, provisioning, disruptions, cloud provider operations, spot interruptions, NodePool capacity, and estimated cost.

display.name: nodepool
display.description: Karpenter NodePool name. Applied only to panels whose metrics carry a nodepool label.

display.name: capacity_type
display.description: on-demand, spot or reserved. Values are discovered across all Karpenter metrics, so capacity types your cluster never launches can appear in the list.

display.name: zone
display.description: Availability zone. The value flexible comes from the scheduler's effective-zone metric and is not a real AZ.

display.name: Nodes in Cluster State
display.description: Total nodes Karpenter is tracking in its cluster state cache, Karpenter-managed and unmanaged. Unlabelled gauge, so it is safe to aggregate with max across replicas: only the leader emits it.

display.name: Cluster State Synced
display.description: 1 when Karpenter's in-memory cluster state matches the API server, 0 when it has drifted. A sustained 0 means provisioning and disruption decisions are being made on stale data.

display.name: Karpenter-Managed Nodes
display.description: Nodes provisioned by Karpenter, from the nodes resource_type of karpenter_nodepools_usage. Compare with Nodes in Cluster State to see what share of the cluster Karpenter owns.

display.name: Unschedulable Pods
display.description: Pods Karpenter's provisioner cannot place. A non-zero value that does not clear means no NodePool or instance type satisfies the pods' requirements, or a limit has been hit.

display.name: Cluster Utilization by Resource
display.description: Percentage of allocatable capacity consumed by pod requests, per resource type. This is the signal consolidation acts on: low CPU or memory utilization is what makes a node a consolidation candidate.

display.name: Allocatable CPU: Karpenter-Managed vs Unmanaged
display.description: Allocatable CPU cores split by the managed label. Karpenter exports karpenter_nodes_* for every node in the cluster, and managed=true marks the ones it provisioned. Deliberately left unfiltered by the nodepool variable, because unmanaged nodes carry an empty nodepool label.

display.name: Karpenter Build Info
display.description: Running Karpenter version and Go toolchain, from karpenter_build_info. More than one version row means a rollout is mid-flight or replicas disagree.

display.name: Nodes Created
display.description: Nodes launched by Karpenter per interval, by NodePool and zone. Uses increase rather than a per-second rate because node launches are human-paced: a rate renders as unreadable fractions.

display.name: NodeClaims Created
display.description: NodeClaims created per interval, by NodePool and creation reason. A NodeClaim is Karpenter's request for capacity, so this leads Nodes Created; a gap between the two points at launch failures.

display.name: Scheduler Queue Depth
display.description: Pods waiting to be scheduled, by controller. Aggregated with max across the per-run scheduling_id label, which would otherwise add a new series for every scheduling simulation.

display.name: Unschedulable Pods Over Time
display.description: Unschedulable pod count by controller. Read together with Pending Pods by Effective Zone to tell a capacity shortfall from a topology constraint that no zone can satisfy.

display.name: Pending Pods by Effective Zone
display.description: Pending pods grouped by their effective zone constraint. flexible means any zone will do; none means pod topology, volume zones and topology spread have no valid intersection, so no node can ever satisfy them.

display.name: Pod Bound Duration
display.description: Time from pod creation until Karpenter binds it to a node. This is the end-user-visible scheduling latency and includes any wait for a new node to join.

display.name: Pod Provisioning Startup Duration (p95)
display.description: Time from Karpenter deciding a pod can schedule until the pod is running, so it measures Karpenter's own provisioning path rather than cluster-wide scheduling delay.

display.name: Longest Pod Unbound Wait by Namespace
display.description: Worst current wait, per namespace, for a pod that has not been bound yet. A value that climbs without clearing is the earliest sign that provisioning is stuck.

display.name: Pods by Phase
display.description: Pod count by phase from karpenter_pods_state. Grouping by phase collapses the metric's per-pod name, node and owner labels, which are far too granular to chart directly.

display.name: Disruption Decisions by Decision & Reason
display.description: Voluntary disruption decisions Karpenter acted on, split by decision (delete, replace) and reason (empty, underutilized, drifted, expired). This is the authoritative consolidation counter.

display.name: Disruption Decisions by NodePool
display.description: The same decisions attributed to a NodePool, which is what you need to tell whether one NodePool's budget or consolidation policy is driving all the churn.

display.name: Nodes Eligible for Disruption by Reason
display.description: Nodes Karpenter currently considers disruptable. Eligible is not the same as disrupted: budgets, do-not-disrupt annotations and PDBs all gate the step from here to an actual decision.

display.name: Allowed Disruptions by NodePool & Reason
display.description: How many nodes may be disrupted concurrently, per NodePool and reason, as computed from disruption budgets. Note that this metric capitalises its reason values (Empty, Underutilized) while the eligible-nodes and decisions metrics use lowercase.

display.name: Nodes Consuming Disruption Budget
display.description: Nodes currently occupying budget slots. When this sits at the Allowed Disruptions ceiling, budgets are the thing throttling consolidation.

display.name: Nodes Drained
display.description: Nodes whose pods Karpenter finished evicting, per interval and NodePool. Draining precedes termination, so a plateau here with no matching terminations points at a PDB or a stuck pod.

display.name: Nodes Terminated
display.description: Nodes removed by Karpenter, per interval, by NodePool and zone.

display.name: NodeClaims Disrupted by Reason
display.description: NodeClaims disrupted per interval, by NodePool, reason and capacity type. Splitting on capacity_type separates voluntary consolidation of on-demand capacity from spot reclamation.

display.name: NodeClaims Terminated
display.description: NodeClaims terminated per interval, by NodePool, capacity type and zone.

filter.expression: nodepool IN $nodepool AND capacity_type IN $capacity_type AND zone IN $zone

display.name: Disruption Decision Evaluation Duration
display.description: How long Karpenter spends evaluating a disruption decision, by reason and consolidation type. Rising p95 here, together with Consolidation Timeouts, means the consolidation algorithm is running out of time on this cluster's size.

display.name: Consolidation Timeouts
display.description: Times the consolidation algorithm gave up before finishing, by consolidation type. Any sustained non-zero value means Karpenter is leaving consolidation opportunities on the table.

display.name: NodeClaim Termination Duration (p95)
display.description: Time to fully terminate a NodeClaim, by NodePool. Long tails usually mean drain is blocked rather than that the cloud provider is slow; compare with CloudProvider Call Latency to tell them apart.

display.name: CloudProvider Error Rate by Method & Error
display.description: Errors returned by EC2 API calls, per interval, by method and error type. This is where insufficient-capacity, throttling and IAM failures surface before they show up as unschedulable pods.

display.name: CloudProvider Call Latency by Method
display.description: Latency of Karpenter's EC2 API calls. Sustained p95 growth on Create or Delete directly slows provisioning and termination.

display.name: CloudProvider Call Rate by Method
display.description: EC2 API calls per second by method, from the observation counter of the duration histogram. Useful for spotting a reconcile loop hammering the API before AWS starts throttling it.

display.name: Cluster State Unsynced Time
display.description: How long cluster state has been out of sync. Anything beyond a brief spike after a restart means Karpenter is deciding on stale data.

display.name: Scheduling Simulation Duration by Controller
display.description: Duration of the scheduling simulations Karpenter runs for both provisioning and disruption. These are CPU-bound and grow with cluster and pod count.

display.name: Interruption Messages Received by Type
display.description: SQS interruption messages Karpenter consumed, by message type. spot_interrupted and instance_terminated are the ones that cost you capacity; no_op is routine noise. Empty unless interruption handling is enabled with an SQS queue.

display.name: Interruption Message Queue Duration (p95)
display.description: How long an interruption message sat in SQS before Karpenter processed it. Spot gives roughly two minutes of notice, so latency here eats directly into the time available to drain gracefully.

display.name: NodePool Usage as % of Limit
display.description: Provisioned resources as a percentage of the NodePool's configured limit. Approaching 100% is why Karpenter stops launching nodes and pods start piling up as unschedulable. Only resource types that have an explicit limit appear here.

display.name: NodePool Hourly Cost Estimate
display.description: Karpenter's own estimate of the hourly cost of a NodePool's nodes, including NodeOverlay adjustments. Karpenter's pricing view, not a billing source.

display.name: CPU Requests as % of Allocatable
display.description: Pod CPU requests over node allocatable CPU, split by the managed label. Persistently low values on managed=true nodes are what consolidation should be reclaiming.

display.name: Node System Overhead
display.description: Capacity reserved for system daemons, the gap between a node's capacity and its allocatable value. CPU is in cores and memory in bytes, so the two series are not on a comparable scale.

display.name: Oldest Karpenter Node Age by NodePool
display.description: Age of the oldest Karpenter-managed node per NodePool. Compare against the NodePool's expireAfter: nodes drifting past it should be showing up as expired in the disruption panels.
